CodeMap is a Roslyn-powered MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that turns any MCP-compatible AI agent into a semantic code navigator for C#, VB.NET, and F# solutions.

Instead of reading source files, agents call 26 focused MCP tools to query symbols, call graphs, type hierarchies, and architectural facts (HTTP endpoints, config keys, DB tables, DI registrations, middleware, retry policies, log templates) — directly from a Roslyn-built semantic index stored in memory-mapped binary segments (v2 engine, zero native DLL dependencies). Mixed-language solutions (.sln / .slnx containing both C# and VB.NET projects) are indexed in a single pass. SQLite fallback available via CODEMAP_ENGINE=sqlite.

Average token savings: 90%+ vs raw file reading. On production codebases: 95–99%+.

Key capabilities:
- symbols.search / symbols.get_card / symbols.get_context — find and understand any symbol
- graph.trace_feature — full annotated feature flow in one call
- refs.find / graph.callers / graph.callees — precise reference and call chain navigation
- codemap.summarize / codemap.export / index.diff — codebase overview and semantic PR diffs
- Workspace mode — see uncommitted edits via incremental overlay (~63ms refresh)
- Shared baseline cache — index once, reuse across machines (CODEMAP_CACHE_DIR)

Usage: add 'codemap-mcp' as an MCP server in your AI agent config. See README for setup.

Truvio Buying Assistant: an AI buying assistant for Dynamicweb 10 storefronts, by JustDynamics.

A shopper describes what they need in plain language ("everything to open a 20,000 gallon pool", "1,800 sq ft gable roof, full tear-off", "replacement union set for a 1 HP pump", "same as my last order but for 32 squares"). The assistant searches the live catalog, sizes the job with your own rules, prices every line at that customer's prices with quantity breaks, checks stock per location and returns a cart-ready proposal with a live activity feed, the reasoning per line, and one "Add all to cart" button. The shopper can change quantities or drop lines (re-priced live with quantity breaks) before adding, and follow-up questions refine the same, edited proposal. Everything the model proposes is re-priced by the platform before it reaches the cart.

SET UP WITH DYNAMO (recommended)
After installing and restarting, open Dynamo (the backend AI assistant) and type:

    /truvio-buying-assistant-setup

or simply "Set up the buying assistant for this site". The app ships a Dynamo skill that checks the installation, reads your catalog, drafts the business instructions and skills for your products, places the assistant on the product details page and on an "Ask" landing page, walks you through the one manual step (the Anthropic API key, unless Dynamo's own key can be reused) and verifies a first storefront run with you.

WHAT IS IN THE BOX
- "Buying Assistant" paragraph (item type Truvio_BuyingAssistant) with editor fields for copy, example prompts, mode (product page or standalone), business instructions and skills ("## Skill: ..." sections that say when they apply and how to size that kind of request).
- Built-in tools that run inside the host: catalog search, product detail with specs and variants, price at quantity (price providers, customer agreements and quantity breaks apply), stock per stock location, categories, the shopper's account and cart, recent orders for reorders.
- Optional MCP connection (Direct from the host, or Anthropic's connector) with a tool allowlist and a write guard, so the assistant can use backend tools such as documentation search.
- Settings screen under Settings > Apps > Buying Assistant: API key, model (claude-opus-5-5 by default), effort, global instructions and skills, search query, MCP, limits, anonymous access, logging.
- Swift 2 paragraph layout, JS and CSS served by the app; a status file Dynamo can read to verify the configuration and the last run.
